A big one under the hood: the share index cache is much smaller and never throws anything away
for its age, Health fills itself in, and usnfetch finally keeps to your provider's connection
limit however many downloads run at once. Plus a collapsible menu and some console colours, just
for fun.

**Upgrading:** replace `usnfetch.exe` and start it as usual. The first time, it converts the
share indexes it already has to the new, smaller format in the background, without downloading
anything. That takes a few minutes for a big cache. A share you open meanwhile may wait a moment
while the index being converted finishes.

## A much smaller index cache that doesn't expire

- **About half the size.** Indexes don't keep what they only needed while being built any more,
  and they store a few things more compactly. A 2.3 GB index for a 3-million-file share is now
  1.26 GB. My whole cache went from 22 GB to under 16 GB.
- **Nothing expires by age.** Shares never change, so there was no reason to rebuild an index
  every 3 days. The ones you used most recently are kept, up to a limit you can set under
  Settings → Downloads → Advanced (20 GB to start with).
- **Past the limit, the file list stays.** Instead of being deleted, the least recently used are
  cut down to their file list and zipped. Browsing and searching those shares is still instant,
  and the rest is fetched again only when you preview, check or download something.
- **Box art you've seen is kept**, so a gallery opens again without going back to Usenet.
- On Windows, idle indexes are also compressed by Windows itself. The System page shows what it
  all takes.

## Health that fills itself in

- Importing a list asks your provider about each new link, one small request apiece. Dead links
  show up as **Gone** right away, the rest as **Link OK**.
- Opening a share checks a sample of its files by itself, so Health becomes **Available**,
  **Partial** or **Missing** for everything you browse.
- Links imported before you added a provider get checked once you add one. Tick some and press
  **Check links** to check them again.
- The download review checks pasted links too, and leaves out any that are gone.
- Health sorts, and the line above the list counts the gone ones.

## See what you've already opened

A new **Opened** column marks every share you've looked at and whether its index is still
cached. Filter by opened, cached or not opened yet, or sort by recently opened.

## Connections, shared properly

Every download used to open your provider's full connection count of its own, so with a few
running side by side usnfetch asked for far more than the provider allows, and the extras were
turned away. Now each provider has one budget, its connection setting, shared by everything:
downloads, previews, checks and index fetches. Downloads use the lot and hand a few back while
you preview or check something. Easynews allows 60, so that's what to enter for it.

## Look

- The menu on the left folds down to icons with the button at its foot. The menu across the top
  is gone.
- Console colour schemes in Settings → Appearance: Super Famicom, N64, Game Boy, Game Gear, Mega
  Drive and Dreamcast.

## Also

- The share log says what kind of share it is in plain words, and the app talks about `usn://`
  shares rather than naming another product.
